overturned.target: process sandbox (deterministic work-accounting / count_lines cost model)
overturned.why: The isolation (Landlock/seccomp/uid, FS, net, exec) genuinely holds, but sandbox/boot.py places the line counter and the broker send/recv in the agent's own namespace by design. The cost model is a trust-domain placement error (measure outside the agent process); the metering is REDESIGN at root, not only in the downstream consumers. Keep the isolation at RETAIN/REPAIR.

EXTEND implies functional-but-incomplete. probes(), gate_metrics, suite and KNOWN_OPEN do not import; 9/10 declared modules absent; no test imports it. Not functional, so IMPLEMENT (consistent with the W.3/W.4/W.5/W.9 requirement verdicts).

Note sharpened: forbid_in_this_process has ZERO call sites in src and _FORBIDDEN_HERE is empty at runtime, so the documented process latch is inert (the real-world __init__ docstring overstates defense-in-depth).
Consumers-of-sandbox-figures REDESIGN is justified (metering forgery reproduced).
No verdict in the original report was found to be unjustifiably harsh.
critical_findings: Amendment (a) is undermined beyond the default flag: cost/compute (the key 'real observable consequence' the amendment says to keep) is agent-forgeable, and the in-process learner can read the grader's answer key; an agent here would learn to zero its meter and read the holdout, not transferable work. Flipping reward_mode to observation_only is necessary but far from sufficient.
Reference Gym ExperienceEnv leaks hidden ground truth (rule params + full holdout suite) to any in-process learner via env.env._engine.sc: breaks OO.4 and W.2 for the primary RL learner path.
Sandbox deterministic cost model is self-reported by agent code (counter + broker protocol in __main__): REDESIGN, and the 4.0 post-check cannot detect the forgery.
